A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dual-End Consistency Model (DE-CM). Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F are readable and matchable, including material relocated in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original ImageNet and text-to-image experiments, training-efficiency comparisons, loss ablations and appendix hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds author-reproduced AlphaFlow/CMT comparisons and a GAN-integration study.

M1.justification: Appendix D introduces an experimental DE-CM + GAN training variant. This is a limited adaptation: the main DE-CM objectives, Algorithm 1 and inference formulation remain unchanged, and the GAN integration is not specified in detail.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet-256 class-to-image generation and text-to-image generation using the same stated data coverage. The new comparisons and GAN experiment introduce no distinct dataset, task or input scenario.

E2.justification: New Table 3 adds AlphaFlow and CMT, including author reproductions, as evaluated comparators. Table D.2 adds comparison with DE-CM + GAN. Existing comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged; iMF, BOOT and sLCT are discussed but not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: New Table D.2 compares training with and without GAN integration at 100 and 200 epochs, evaluated at 1, 2, 4 and 50 NFE. These are added experimental conditions, not revisions to the retained benchmark settings. Table 3 does not specify detailed reproduction protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds an analysis of whether GAN integration helps convergence while preserving performance across sampling budgets. Existing loss ablations, hyperparameter studies, efficiency analyses and qualitative comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 3 reports reproduced 1/2-NFE FIDs of 2.24/1.71 for AlphaFlow and 2.71/1.68 for CMT. Table D.2 adds GAN results: at 200 epochs, DE-CM versus DE-CM + GAN yields 1-NFE FID 1.74 versus 1.72, but 50-NFE FID 1.28 versus 1.46. Existing benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The main mathematical formulation and Appendix A–B derivations are retained. Section 5.4 discusses existing equations and their relationship to other methods without adding or revising formal definitions, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of stable training through selected trajectories, flexible sampling through N2N mapping, and 1.70 one-step ImageNet FID. Removing a redundant trajectory-selection sentence from the conclusion does not alter these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly attributes later multi-step degradation with GAN integration to its tendency to optimize a single mapping, potentially constraining DE-CM. The existing limitation concerning JVP compatibility and GPU memory remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The GAN study supplies limited additional training-budget information through its 100- and 200-epoch checkpoints. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters and prompts remain unchanged. No discriminator architecture, GAN loss configuration or detailed AlphaFlow/CMT reproduction instructions are added.

R1.justification: New Section 5.4 adds substantive comparisons with sLCT, BOOT, iMF, AlphaFlow and CMT, with five corresponding references. It distinguishes DE-CM's stability rationale and continuous-time N2N formulation while retaining the earlier research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds Section 5.4 and acknowledgments, moves references before the supplementary material, makes appendix cross-references explicit and lightly shortens the conclusion. Most existing prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 3 and D.2, renumbers the original loss-ablation table as Table 4, and adjusts spacing and placement around the added material. Existing figures, qualitative image grids and retained table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 5.4 and Table 3 improve comparison with recent methods, while Table D.2 adds useful evidence that GAN integration trades small one-step benefits for poorer later multi-step performance. These are limited gains over the retained scientific contribution. Sparse reproduction and GAN implementation details constrain the strength and reproducibility of the new evidence.
